newsitem.title: GREECE: GREEK ALPHA CREDIT TO UP EQUITY BY 72.6BLN DRS.
newsitem.headline: GREEK ALPHA CREDIT TO UP EQUITY BY 72.6BLN DRS.

text.p: Greek Alpha Credit Bank will raise its share capital by 72.6 billion drachmas via a rights and a one-for-four bonus issue following the approval by its annual shareholders meeting on Thursday.

Existing shareholders will have the right to buy one new share for every four outstanding at 11,000 drachmas. The bank will proceed with a one-for-four bonus share distribution resulting from a capitalisation of reserves.
The subscription period commences April 7 and runs through May 9.

Alpha Credit Bank will use proceeds to increase its market share by extending its branch and ATM network. It will buy information systems, participate in the share capital increase of firms belonging to its group and develop new products.
Board chairman Yannis Costopoulos told the general shareholders meeting that the bank would continue to look for opportunities to be provided by the anticipated shakeout in Greece's financial sector.

Gross operating profit rose 19.6 percent to 166.3 billion drachmas in 1996, pretax profits increased 18.8 percent to 54 billion drachmas and pretax profits after minority interests posted an increase of 19.9 percent to 47.2 billion, said Costopoulos.
"The return on equity stood at 32.2 percent (in 1996) compared to 31.6 percent and return on assets at 2.1 percent against 2.3 percent," said Costopoulos.
Earnings per share increased 19.9 percent to 1.788 drachmas in 1996 from 1.491 drachmas in 1995, he added.
Alpha Credit Bank will distribute a dividend per share of 925 drachmas for fiscal 1996, up 12 percent on 1995, said Costopoulos.

Eleven new branches were added to Alpha Credit Bank's branch network in 1996 to reach 190 at end-96. The bank plans to have 200 branches at the end of 1997 and expand its ATM network which numbers 350 ATMs today.

"The Bank was very active abroad in 1996 as well," said Costopoulos. "Alpha Bank London and Banca Bucuresti show continuous growth and we have taken a licence to open a branch in Tirana scheduled to be operational by end-1997 provided that the situation in the country is stabilised."
The Greek economy improved in 1996 as evidenced by lower inflation and the downward trend in interest rates, said Costopoulos.
"Increased competition in the banking system contributed to the fall in interest rates," he said. --Dimitris Kontogiannis, Athens Newsroom +301 3311812-4
